# glinet_lan_config (Resource)

Manages the address and the DHCP server of the LAN or of the guest network of the router (`lan.set_config` in the router API). Use one instance of this resource for each network. Both networks always exist on the router, so create takes over the network. The web UI writes the address group (`ip`, `netmask`, `ap_isolation`) and the DHCP group (the other attributes) in two calls. The provider sends a group only when one of its values differs: on create from the values of the router, on update from the state. It sends the address group first. A create whose values are equal to those of the router sends no write. **Danger:** each write to the LAN configuration, also for the `guest` network and also a write that changes nothing, makes the router restart its Wi-Fi a few seconds later. When the uplink of the router is a Wi-Fi repeater, the uplink and each VPN on it can drop and may not come back without a manual reconnect or a reboot. This was measured on a GL-AXT1800 with firmware 4.7.0. A change of `ip` or `netmask` of the `lan` network changes the address of the router. The provider then loses its connection, so the write of the DHCP group and the read after the write fail: change the provider `host` to the new address and apply again. Also a wrong DHCP configuration or a disabled DHCP server of the `lan` network can cut the access to the router of the clients that get their address by DHCP. The router does not accept a network that contains the address of the other network or of the uplink (errors -7, -8, -9). The write of this resource was not tested on a router; the parameters come from the router's web UI. Destroy removes the resource from the Terraform state and does not change the router.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "glinet_lan_config" "guest" {
  interface    = "guest"
  ip           = "192.168.9.1"
  netmask      = "255.255.255.0"
  ap_isolation = true
  dhcp_enabled = true
  dhcp_start   = "192.168.9.100"
  dhcp_end     = "192.168.9.249"
  lease_time   = "12h"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `ap_isolation` (Boolean) Whether the Wi-Fi clients of the network cannot reach each other (`ap_isolate` in the router API).
- `dhcp_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the DHCP server of the network is enabled (`enable` in the router API). When it is `false`, the provider sends only `enable: 0`, as the web UI does, and the other DHCP attributes cannot be set.
- `interface` (String) The network: `lan` or `guest` (`interface` in the router API). Changing it replaces the resource.
- `ip` (String) Private IPv4 address of the router in the network (`ip` in the router API). It cannot be the network or the broadcast address.
- `netmask` (String) Netmask of the network, for example `255.255.255.0` (`netmask` in the router API). The prefix length must be 8 to 30, at least 12 for a `172.*` address and at least 16 for a `192.*` address.

### Optional

- `dhcp_end` (String) Last IPv4 address that the DHCP server gives, for example `192.168.8.249` (`end` in the router API). Must be in the network. Required when `dhcp_enabled` is `true`.
- `dhcp_start` (String) First IPv4 address that the DHCP server gives, for example `192.168.8.100` (`start` in the router API). Must be in the network and less than `dhcp_end`. Required when `dhcp_enabled` is `true`.
- `dns` (List of String) One or two IPv4 addresses of the DNS servers that the DHCP server gives (`dns` in the router API). When it is not set, the clients get the router.
- `gateway` (String) IPv4 address of the gateway that the DHCP server gives (`gateway` in the router API). When it is not set, the clients get the router.
- `lease_time` (String) DHCP lease time in hours or minutes, for example `12h` or `720m`, from 2 minutes to 71582788 minutes (`leasetime` in the router API). The provider sends it in minutes, as the web UI does. Two values with the same duration, such as `12h` and `720m`, are equal: when the router reports a lease time with the same duration as the state, the state keeps its value. Required when `dhcp_enabled` is `true`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is the network: "lan" or "guest".
terraform import glinet_lan_config.guest guest
```
